subject: procD.allometry for PC scores and centroid size

messages.author: 0115fa6682bc8072
messages.subject: procD.allometry for PC scores and centroid size
parts:
Hi all,

I used the function procD.allometry to directly analyze the relationship between PC scores and centroid size by putting all PC scores of one PC into a vector: The code is:


#PC1_score is a vector that contains all PC1 scores. 
reg_PC1 <- procD.allometry(PC1_score~Csize, itr=9999)
summary(reg_PC1)


The result looks OK:
                  Df       SS             MS                 Rsq               F              Z           Pr(>F)  
log(size)    1        0.012170   0.0121696       0.13019       7.0348     1.4381   0.015 *
Residuals 47       0.081306   0.0017299       0.86981                       
Total          48       0.093476


I wonder if I can actually do this test using the "procD. allometry" function in this way. Thank you very much for your suggestions! 

Best regards,
Charles Zhang

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] procD.allometry for PC scores and centroid size
parts:
Charles,

 

One should not simplify the response (Y) variable to a single dimension when the analyses are explicitly designed for multivariate data. The permutation-based approaches in geomorph and RRPP have been vetted for multivariate data, so the simplification is unnecessary (and can miss patterns in one’s data, or generate misleading patterns not found in the full dataspace).

 

Dean

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.allometry for PC scores and centroid size
parts:
Charles, to augment on Deans comment, in addition to be a statistically and methodologically better choice, working in full shape space will also allow you to directly visualize (full, as Dean comments) shape changes related to size, which is not the case with PC1.

And as a practical note, notice that procD.allometry has been deprecated in the last version of geomorph, and substituted by more general procedures through procD.lm. The vignette now included in the package provides very thorough support for how to implement analyses previously carried out using other procD.family functions, see, e.g. the new plotAllometry function for visualizing allometric variation, in combination with picknplot or plotRefToTarget for obtaining deformation grids in allometric space.

Antigoni
